premise: You've just moved into a creaky old housing compound in Chengdu, and on your very first night a round white stray cat sits outside your door like it pays the rent. Every neighbour seems to know exactly who this cat is, and nobody will tell you. To find out, you'll need to order noodles, brave the pharmacy, ride the metro across town and make a whole compound's worth of friends, in Chinese.
question: Why does the stray cat keep coming to your door, and whose cat is it really? (Answer: it is 汤圆, who lived in your flat with its previous tenant, 陈婆婆, until she moved across the city to live with her daughter. The cat stayed behind, the neighbours have fed it in turns ever since, and they quietly agreed to wait and see whether it would choose the new tenant. In volume 7 陈婆婆 visits, sees the cat asleep on your doormat, and officially hands 汤圆 over to you.)

cast.voice: Loud and motherly; says 哎呀 a lot, calls you 小马, asks 吃了没有? every time she sees you and answers her own questions before you can
Short blunt sentences of two or three words (好。不行。等一下。), ends things with 嗯, never smiles but always helps
Speaks slowly and carefully to you, repeats key words, checks with 你懂吗? and likes to teach you one new word each time
Fast and cheerful, always asks 要辣的吗? and 几两?, sprinkles in 巴适 and other Sichuan words then translates them into standard Mandarin
Gentle and old-fashioned, polite set phrases like 麻烦你了 and 不好意思, talks to the cat as if it were a person

volumes.beat: You collect your keys from the property office, sort out the electricity card with 张阿姨's loud help, and come home to find a round white cat waiting at your door as if it lives there, while 张阿姨 only says 哎呀, it came back.

Determined to feed the cat properly, you meet 李晓雨 at the pet shop to buy cat food, then start sneezing and have to describe your symptoms at a pharmacy, where you learn it is only dust from your unaired flat.
Ordering breakfast noodles at 刘老板's shop, you notice he puts aside a little plain chicken every morning, and the gate guard 周师傅 lets slip that the cat has a name but refuses to say more.
The cat finally lets you pick it up and you find a faded collar tag reading 汤圆 with your own flat number on it, and 张阿姨 admits the cat used to live in your flat with 陈婆婆, who moved away last year.

After your first morning teaching at a language school, you take the metro and a bus across Chengdu to the address 周师傅 grudgingly gives you, find 陈婆婆 in her daughter's flat, and she asks how 汤圆 is eating.

汤圆 does not come to your door, so you print lost-cat posters at a copy shop and the whole compound, from 刘老板 to 周师傅, joins you asking shopkeepers and searching every stairwell until 李晓雨 spots it stuck on a bicycle shed roof.
陈婆婆 visits for a neighbourhood hotpot you help shop for, sees 汤圆 asleep on your doormat, explains that the neighbours were waiting to see if it would choose you, and gives you its old bowl.
